summary: B.C. cuts TFL 30's AAC 17.6%, Pennsylvania hardwood sales close this week, Pacific Northwest federal auctions bunch up after Labor Day, and a 4,833-acre Washington timber portfolio remains active.
socialText: B.C. cuts TFL 30's AAC 17.6%; Pennsylvania offers a 692-MBF oak sale Wednesday; a 4,833-acre Washington timber portfolio is still active after its original bid date.
strikingText: B.C. just cut TFL 30's allowable annual cut 17.6% to 340,000 m³—and explicitly removed more economically marginal ground from the harvestable land base. Fibre supply is contracting not just biologically, but economically.

summary: LP's Jasper OSB curtailment, Southern log-trucking entry barriers, Oregon timberland pricing, hardwood slab data, forest-road research, and field tools.
socialText: LP is idling 475M sq. ft. of Jasper OSB capacity; a 573-driver Southern study puts insurance and experience at the center of the log-truck bottleneck; a 1,120-acre Oregon timber tract asks $5.7M.
strikingText: About 80% of Southern log-truck drivers surveyed don't want to leave the business, yet only 9% of non-third-party drivers would consider third-party hauling without better pay and benefits. The bottleneck looks more like entry economics than retention.

summary: Washington salvage authority, Coosa Pines pulpwood impacts, Tahoe Forest Products financing, lumber prices, Western contractor opportunities, WOTUS, and new tools.
socialText: Washington lifts fast-track salvage sales to $2M; Coosa Pines' closure sends pine pulpwood stumpage toward zero; Tahoe Forest Products lands $50M in USDA-backed financing.
